newsitem.title: GERMANY: LUFTHANSA CARGO SEES MORE FORWARDER, SHIPPER.
newsitem.headline: LUFTHANSA CARGO SEES MORE FORWARDER, SHIPPER.

text.p: Three-way talks between airlines, forwarders and shippers will become increasingly common in the air cargo industry, a senior Lufthansa Cargo AG manager forecast.
Stefan Lauer, Lufthansa Cargo board member for sales and marketing, said the airline was seeking a new era of improved co-operation between shippers, forwarders and carriers to end years of mistrust.

"More than 80 percent of Lufthansa Cargo turnover comes from the air cargo agents distribution channel and nothing should change that in future," he said at a meeting with the Federation of German Industry (BDI) air transport committee.

"But we reserve the right to talk to shipping clients individually. Three-way talks between shippers, forwarders and Lufthansa Cargo, the so-called tripartite approach, will gain significance in future," a BDI statement quoted him as saying.
Freight forwarders have traditionally been very wary of direct airline-air cargo shipper talks out of fears they could be cut out of the logistics chain.

Lauer said Lufthansa would introduce barcoding as the basis for a worldwide tracking and tracing system this year and all shipments worldwide would have to carry the standardised IATA labels from next spring.
The airline's improved Flash express service with time and performance guarantees was one possible co-operation model with air cargo shippers, he added.
